Subject: Sizing for Dedicated capacity - DataNova

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, we're evaluating a Dedicated GPU pool for production inference (primary models: instruction-tuned 30B / 70B variants). A few things we need to figure out before we can move to procurement:

- Recommended pool size for our workload
- Typical throughput guarantees (p99/p95 latency targets) and burst behavior
- Commit structure and discounting (12 vs 24 month, reserved v. on-demand)

High-level context:
- User-facing chat product, western US region
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~180k requests/day
- Average request: ~1,000 tokens total (400 prompt + 600 generation)
- Peak traffic: ~60 concurrent active sessions (short peaks up to 90)
- Most calls use 8k context; some longer sessions (up to 32k) are rare (<=5% of traffic)

Can you share a ballpark for the recommended pool (GPU type and count), and a draft commit/discount structure we can bring to procurement? We're trying to size monthly committed spend to compare vs. cloud-managed endpoints.

Also looping Tom (infra) and procurement address.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of ML Ops, DataNova

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear numbers; very helpful. Quick follow-ups so our sizing recommendation is tight:

1) What model repo & quantization profile do you plan to serve (70B FP16 / int8 quant)? If you're exploring int8 quant, throughput per GPU changes materially.
2) Can you share average tokens returned vs prompt tokens separately? (you gave combined — just want split if possible)
3) Any hard SLOs for 95/99 latency we need to guarantee for the contract (example: p95 < 350ms for <1k tokens)?

I'm attaching a short questionnaire that helps map to our throughput estimates. If you can fill and send back, we'll produce a 1-page Dedicated proposal with recommended pool size, cost, and commit tiers.

Marissa —

Thanks, answered inline below and in the attached questionnaire.

1) Models: primarily 70B instruction-tuned; plan to serve two flavors: FP16 (baseline) and an int8-quantized variant for lower-latency internal endpoints. Production will start on FP16, moving to int8 for endpoints where quality is acceptable.

2) Token split: average prompt 400 tokens, average generation 600 tokens. We estimated the 1,000 token total previously.

3) SLOs: goal is p95 < 450ms for responses up to 800 generated tokens; p99 is a softer target (we can tolerate up to ~900ms for rare cases). For longer 32k contexts we accept higher latency and can route to a larger-context fallback pool.

Traffic notes: steady-state 180k/day (~2.1 req/s average); typical concurrency 40-60; sustained peaks up to 90 concurrent sessions. Weekend load ~35% lower.

Questionnaire attached (filled).

--
Sarah

Sarah / Tom —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the completed questionnaire. Based on your traffic profile and model choices, here's a proposed Dedicated plan and the negotiation-friendly commit structure you asked for. Full numbers attached (commit-pricing-model.xlsx) and a short one-page PDF proposal (RDW-Dedicated-Proposal-DN-v1.pdf).

Executive summary (baseline -> peak):
- GPU type: H100 (preferred) for best throughput on 70B FP16; int8 gains handled by runtime where applicable
- Baseline recommended pool: 6 x H100 GPUs (this supports ~2.5 - 3.5 req/s for 1k-token interactions per GPU when optimized, delivering steady-state capacity for your average load with headroom for autoscaling)
- Peak sizing & burst: add burst capacity to 9 x H100 for sustained traffic spikes (we can configure burst autoscaling policy + pre-warmed instances to keep p95 latency targets)
- Long-context fallback: keep a small 1-2 GPU pool configured with extended memory/LLM runtime for rare 32k calls (route <=5% traffic)

Throughput & latency expectations (approx):
- With 6x H100, expected average throughput: ~15-21 req/s aggregate (approx 2.5–3.5 req/s per GPU) for 1k-token use-cases, p95 < 400–450ms for typical calls
- With 9x H100 (burst): aggregate ~27–31 req/s, p95 improves under bursts due to reduced queueing
- Note: int8 variants can increase per-GPU throughput ~20–40% depending on quality settings. We'll account for that in the final tuning pass.

Commit / pricing (draft):
- 12-month reserved: base list $X per H100_GPU/month (see XLSX). Offer: 15% discount off list for 6 GPU commit (monthly billing).
- 24-month reserved: 20% discount for a 6 GPU commit; or 18% discount if you commit to 9 GPUs for 12 months.
- Upfront annual prepay: an additional 2–3% discount if paid annually upfront.
- Ramp & sample credits: we can provide a 30-day ramp credit (one-time) equivalent to ~10% of the first month's committed spend to cover tuning and rollout risk.

Operational guarantees & terms:
- SLA: 99.5% uptime on dedicated control plane; per-request latency guarantees are operational targets with runbook-backed fallback to smaller, lower-cost variants if latency SLOs are violated during extreme events.
- Capacity overrides: burst policies will be documented and limited to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
- Review clause: 60-day performance review at the 3-month mark to rebaseline pool size if production traffic deviates >25% from initial estimates.

Next steps:
1) If this looks reasonable, we'll produce a formal quote and a DocuSign-ready order form.
2) Decide on commit term (12 v 24) and whether you want the 9-GPU peak provision included in the monthly committed baseline or as a burst add-on.

Attachments: RDW-Dedicated-Proposal-DN-v1.pdf (pdf), commit-pricing-model.xlsx (xlsx)

Tagging Vivek + Lauren for any legal/finance / discount runway input.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. Procurement is likely to want: clear monthly committed spend, an option to include burst capacity in the commit, and a short performance review/exit window. A couple of asks before we send this to procurement:

1) For the 12-month 6x H100 commit, can you stretch to 18–20% discount if we sign within 30 days? Procurement prefers to benchmark a single-year commit first.
2) Can the 30-day ramp credit be applied as a credit against first two invoices instead of a one-time check? That helps with cashflow.
3) Add a 60-day review clause at month 3 with an option to increase pool by 50% with 30-day notice (we want a fast path to scale if adoption spikes).

If you can update the quote with those three items and send a DocuSign link, we'll take this to procurement and legal. Appreciate the flexibility — we like your approach to burst + fallback pools.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of ML Ops, DataNova
